searched: WebSearch for the ECB euro banknote production allocation 2026 and accredited printing works; fetched the ECB's own 'Banknote production' page
outcome: The page says 11 high-security printing works in Europe produce euro banknotes but names none of them. The only allocation given is an example: the French, German and Italian central banks together produced 1.7 billion EUR 50 notes in 2017. No per-denomination NCB allocation table on the page.
next_step: The annual ECB Decision on the approval of the volume of coin issuance / the ECB Guideline on euro banknote production and procurement, and the yearly 'allocation of euro banknote production' decision published in EUR-Lex (e.g. the ECB decision series ECB/2020/xx on the Eurosystem production and procurement scheme), plus the ECB's 'Banknote manufacturer accreditation' register of accredited works.

searched: Bank of Thailand banknote pages: fetched both 'Banknote production' (npt-production) and 'The History of the Note Printing Works'
outcome: The history page names 'the Note Printing Works at the Bank of Thailand' and dates it (authorised 1961, operating 1969, new Nakhon Pathom site 2007); the production page describes the production of Bank of Thailand banknotes step by step but never names the works in body text. Recorded, but no single sentence says 'the Note Printing Works prints the Bank of Thailand's banknotes'.
next_step: The Bank of Thailand annual Banknote Management Group report, or the BOT page 'BOT and Banknotes', which should state the Note Printing Works' formal mandate and annual print volume.

searched: Searched for Casa da Moeda do Brasil printing real banknotes; fetched the Banco Central do Brasil FAQ on the second family of real notes
outcome: The BCB FAQ says the new family was produced 'em parceria com a Casa da Moeda do Brasil - CMB' and that CMB's new banknote printing lines were bought in a 2009 tender, completed 2010. It does not use the word 'print'. Recorded on that wording.
next_step: Casa da Moeda do Brasil's own institutional page or the BCB's 'Meio circulante' annual report, which states the volume of notes CMB delivers to the BCB each year; also the law authorising the BCB to import notes (would name any foreign printer).

searched: Searched Banco de la República for its Imprenta de Billetes; fetched 'Emisión de la moneda legal colombiana'
outcome: The page states the Bank itself carries out the production of banknotes and coins, and the Imprenta de Billetes appears only as a navigation link under Central de Efectivo. No location, no founding date, no volumes.
next_step: The Banco de la República page 'Central de Efectivo' / 'Imprenta de Billetes' (banrep.gov.co/es/billetes-monedas/central-efectivo), which should describe the printing works directly.

searched: Searched NBS for the Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes and Coins (Topčider); fetched the NBS anniversary page on the Institute
outcome: Confirms the Institute makes 'banknotes and coins issued by the NBS' plus products for foreign countries. The word dinar does not appear; no current volumes.
next_step: The NBS Decision on the Institute (ZIN) statute, or the NBS annual report chapter on cash, for current print volumes and any foreign clients.

searched: Searched for the BSP Security Plant Complex; fetched Manila Bulletin 'BSP to print all banknotes'
outcome: Confirms the BSP prints at its own Security Plant Complex in Quezon City (3.098 billion notes in 2019) and that it outsources some printing as a stop-gap, but names no outside printer.
next_step: The BSP annual report or its 'BSP outsourced 62% of banknotes in 2020' reporting, and BSP procurement notices, which would name the foreign printers used (candidates to verify, not assume).

searched: Searched KOMSCO and the Bank of Korea; fetched The Korea Times piece on the state-run mint
outcome: KOMSCO is described as the state-run mint, 'the country's sole manufacturer of banknotes and coins', in close partnership with the Bank of Korea. No explicit 'KOMSCO prints the Bank of Korea's banknotes' sentence and no contract detail.
next_step: KOMSCO's own English site (komsco.com) 'Banknotes' product page, or the Bank of Korea's currency page stating that KOMSCO manufactures won banknotes.

searched: Searched the State Bank of Vietnam and the National Banknote Printing Factory; fetched The Investor's report on its new chairman
outcome: Confirms the factory is 100% state-owned, is responsible for printing banknotes, and that the SBV Governor appoints its chairman and assigns its production plans. Does not say in words 'prints Vietnam's banknotes'.
next_step: The SBV's 'Money issuance' page (sbv.gov.vn/en/money-issuance) or the SBV decision establishing the National Banknote Printing Factory.

searched: Searched Casa de Moneda and the BCRA; fetched Bloomberg Línea on the suspension of banknote printing
outcome: Confirms Casa de Moneda printed 1,000- and 2,000-peso notes for the BCRA under contracts of Nov 2021, Sep 2022 and Feb 2023, stopped on 28 October 2024, and that the 2,000-peso notes had been subcontracted to Spain's Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre. The printer of the 20,000-peso notes imported from China is not named.
next_step: BCRA procurement awards (Boletín Oficial) for the 10,000 and 20,000 peso notes, which would name the Chinese printer rather than leaving it to inference.

searched: Searched for the ECCB polymer series printer; fetched De La Rue's release on the EC$2 polymer note
outcome: Only establishes De La Rue's SAFEGUARD polymer substrate for the EC$2 note and a supplier relationship; the release does not say who printed the EC$2 note or the 2019 all-polymer series. Recorded as substrate only. Note: cb_iso3 set to KNA (ECCB seat, Basseterre) as a placeholder for the currency union.
next_step: The ECCB's own launch documents ('Governor Antoine's statement at launch of EC polymer notes', eccb-centralbank.org) or its tender award for the polymer series, which should name the printer.

searched: Searched the National Bank of Kazakhstan; fetched its subsidiaries page and Landqart's note on the 20,000 tenge
outcome: Both closed positively: the Banknote Factory of the National Bank prints the banknotes, and Landqart supplies the Durasafe substrate for the 20,000 tenge note. Landqart does not state who printed that note.
next_step: None needed for the printer; for the substrate of the full Saka Style series, the National Bank's series documentation would name the substrate per denomination.

outcome: Closed positively for the 5- and 10-quetzal notes. PWPW does not state the contract value, and does not say who prints other Guatemalan denominations.
next_step: Banco de Guatemala procurement awards (Guatecompras) for banknote printing, which would cover the other denominations.

searched: Searched the Central Bank of Egypt's printing house; first fetch of egypttoday.com failed with a client error, then fetched Amwal Al Ghad
outcome: Closed positively: the CBE's Banknote Printing House in the New Administrative Capital prints Egypt's notes. No capacity figures, no opening date.
next_step: Giesecke+Devrient's press release 'G+D wins EUR260 million contract in Egypt' would document the equipment supplier and the facility's build, and the CBE's own announcement would give the opening date and capacity.

searched: Searched the Bulgarian National Bank printing works; fetched Louisenthal's Bulgaria case study
outcome: Closed positively for both Oberthur Fiduciaire AD (BNB production since 2014) and Louisenthal (paper-embedded thread, foil and watermark on the 100-lev note). Louisenthal does not name the paper product, and does not confirm who printed the 100-lev note specifically.
next_step: BNB tender award notices for banknote printing, and the BNB's own 100-lev issue announcement, which should name the printer outright. Bulgaria joins euro banknote production from January 2026, so the ECB allocation document would cover it going forward.

searched: Searched the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan); fetched its NT$200 press release
outcome: Closed positively, but on a December 2001 release naming 'China Engraving & Printing Works'. The plant's current English name is Central Engraving and Printing Plant, and the source does not state its ownership.
next_step: The Central Engraving and Printing Plant's own site (cepp.gov.tw) or a current CBC banknote page, to confirm the present name and that it is a CBC subsidiary.

searched: Searched Banxico's banknote factory; fetched Expansión's explainer
outcome: Closed positively: Banxico makes all its own denominations at factories in Mexico City and El Salto, Jalisco, with printing moved in-house in 1969 from the American Bank Note Company. Source is a news explainer, not a Banxico page.
next_step: Banco de México's own 'Fábrica de Billetes' page or its Billetes y Monedas report, for a primary-source statement and current volumes.

searched: Searched De La Rue contract awards; fetched Currency News on the Denmark award
outcome: Closed positively for both De La Rue (new series, from 2028, minimum six years) and Oberthur Fiduciaire (Danish notes since 2018). Crane Currency is named only for the design and specification contract awarded in 2024, which is not printing. No contract value.
next_step: Danmarks Nationalbank's own press release on the printing contract, which may give the value and the exact start date.

outcome: Closed positively on a quoted statement by a retired BoG Deputy Governor that the cedi is printed by De La Rue. He also refers to past work with security printers in Germany and France without naming them, and no contract value is given.
next_step: The Bank of Ghana annual report's currency printing cost line (GHC 300m+ in 2019 was reported separately) or a BoG procurement notice naming the printer and contract value.
